column3: Package manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-hook-protocol v0.2.1-rc.2: ESM, publishes lib/index.js + lib/types, peer-deps on dsh-shell/dsh-session/cordis, and exports "./src/*" so tests can import source directly.
Bilingual-pair consistency record: per-heading-section hashes of the English and Chinese README blocks; regenerated by `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write`.

Package reference for the shared hook engine: what a hook can do, the six-step pipeline (validate matcher, run, decode, merge, record, drain), design philosophy ("Never throw into the loop"), and the three stated limits (updatedInput parsed but not honored, folded halt has no run-level effect, only the command-hook shape runs).
Chinese translation of the hook-protocol README; head confirms it mirrors the English section-for-section ("概述" = Summary) and the same three Known Limitations.

Decodes a hook process outcome into a dialect-neutral HookOutput: exit 2 = block with stderr as reason, exit 0 may carry JSON, malformed JSON stays plain stdout; applyStructured guards hookSpecificOutput by hookEventName so a block naming a different event has its event-scoped fields discarded.

DetachedRuns tracker for emit-shaped hook runs: an AbortSignal that drain() fires, a Set of in-flight chains pruned on settle, and a drain loop that re-checks after each wave so a run tracked mid-drain is still awaited.

Declaration-merges 'hook/invoked' and 'hook/result' into SessionEventMap as log-only records (no surfaceOp), plus appendHookInvoked/appendHookResult and summarizeStderr with the shared DEFAULT_STDERR_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS = 500.
Public export barrel of the hook-protocol library: types, matcher helpers, parseHookOutput, runHook + DEFAULT_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS, mergeHookOutputs, the event helpers, and createDetachedRuns.

Matcher engine for both dialects: match-all sentinels (absent/''/'*'), Claude literal-or-regex mode (a pure [A-Za-z0-9_|]+ pattern exact-matches pipe-separated alternatives) vs Codex always-regex, invalid regexes become non-matches, and matcherDiagnostic rejects a bad pattern at config-parse time.

Folds every matched hook's outcome into one MergedHookOutcome with deny > ask > allow precedence, reasons collected per rank so only the winning rank's objections surface, the first continue:false stop sticky, and additionalContext/systemMessages accumulated in hook order.

runs a hook through ctx.shell (resolve + execute) with a per-hook timeoutSec overriding DEFAULT_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS = 600000, a caller-owned AbortSignal, optional trailing newline, and converts every infrastructure failure into a HookOutput with no exit code so runHook never throws into the loop.
Dialect-neutral vocabulary: HookDialect ('claude-code'|'codex'), CommandHook, MatcherGroup, MatcherMode, the optional-everything HookOutput, and the hook/* SessionEventMap payload declarations.

Vitest for parseHookOutput: exit-code semantics, the approve/block-only legacy top-level decision (allow/deny/ask there are invalid), permissionDecision overriding it, the hookEventName mismatch and missing-discriminator discards, and structured stdout ignored on exit 2.
Vitest for createDetachedRuns: drain fires the signal, waits for a tracked run, waits for a run tracked WHILE a prior wave settles, and absorbs a rejected chain.
Vitest for the hook/* events: log-only (no surfaceOp), absent matcher omitted, decision falling back to stop/pass, the 500-char stderr summary truncation, and invoked/result correlating by handlerId.

Vitest for matcher semantics: the three match-all sentinels, Claude literal exact-match vs Codex substring-regex on the same 'Bash' pattern, invalid regex as a non-match, the stable diagnostic strings, and selectHookGroups keeping config order.
Vitest for mergeHookOutputs: deny>ask>allow ordering, reasons joined only from blocking hooks and only at the winning rank, the sticky first stop, and context/systemMessages collected in hook order.

Vitest for runHook with a duck-typed recording ShellExecutor: stdin serialization with/without trailing newline, env/cwd threading, timeoutSec vs default, signal passthrough, a null exit code (signal death) decoding as undefined, and an executor rejection becoming a non-blocking error.
TS project: rootDir src, outDir lib/types, project references to vendor/cosmokit, vendor/cordis, packages/shell/shell and packages/core/session.

The CC bridge plugin: registers agent/created, agent/pre-step, tools/pre-execute, tools/post-execute, agent/turn-stopping, subagent/start and subagent/end listeners; maps merged decisions onto PreTool/PostTool/PreStep decisions; builds the per-event stdin payloads; and records hook/invoked + hook/result per hook.

The PythonPtcRuntime plugin (2,382 lines): load-time config gate (platform, integer cpuSeconds, safe-integer addressSpaceMb, timer-clamp bounds, byte budgets vs the frame cap and vs RLIMIT_AS), interpreter resolution and version probe, spawn with a detached process group and fd 3, the log ledger, the settlement ladder, and process-group teardown. Delivers the trusted Python sources to the interpreter as UTF-8 JSON on stdin (PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP_LOADER) so no sandbox-visible temp file and no locale-dependent source encoding is involved.

Host side of the fd-3 protocol (718 lines): the frame unions, the WIRE_FRAME_FIELD_ROLES exhaustive required/optional map, encodeJsonPlain (non-recursive), checkDoneValue (byte + losslessness meter), hasUnsafeIntegerToken (reads the raw text because JSON.parse rounds first), hasNonLosslessNumber, and validateChildFrame which rebuilds every inbound frame instead of passing it through.
Mocks node:child_process so the fd-3 pipe throws EPIPE on the very first boot-frame write, proving a child that cannot be fed settles the run instead of hanging the host.

Cross-language mirror test: spawns a real python3 and compares PROTOCOL_FD, the truncation-marker text, and every public TypedDict's required/optional key sets against WIRE_FRAME_FIELDS; self-skips when python3 is absent.

Proves detachResidual returns a right-sized copy that does not share the source frame's backing store, so a small residual view cannot pin a 1 MiB allocation.

Package reference: the ONNX/Silero CPU provider, the model-origin probe policy (concurrent HEAD, first 2xx wins, fallback on network/http/certificate/integrity but NOT on cancellation or storage), the source list, and the limits (CPU only, INT8 ~239 MB vs FP32 ~938 MB, Windows ARM64 and Linux musl unverified).
Chinese translation of the SenseVoice provider page.
Release-pinned asset lock: the int8 and fp32 SenseVoice ONNX files, tokens.txt and the Silero VAD file, each with an exact byte count, a SHA-256 and a revision-pinned Hugging Face resolve URL.

Schemastery config for the local recognizer: providerId, absolute dataRoot, optional pre-existing modelDirectory/vadModelPath, precision, modelOrigin/modelOrigins with a URL pattern that rejects credentials, and every budget bounded by MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS.

Classifies a download failure into dns/timeout/certificate/storage/network/http/integrity/unknown by walking the error cause chain (including AggregateError) with a visited set for cycles, and exposes a SpeechDownloadError whose public text carries no URL credentials, query strings or raw cause messages.

Plugin entry: rejects relative paths and invalid origins before registering the provider on ctx.speechToText, publishes the disk estimate, and calls worker.inspect() so activation performs no download and starts no worker.

Loads sherpa-onnx OfflineRecognizer + Silero Vad, decodes 16 kHz PCM16, feeds 512-sample windows, and restores the onset a cold VAD reports late by padding the FIRST segment only (Electron memory-cage copies for the VAD output).
Language hints (auto/zh/en/yue/ja/ko) and validateInput, which rejects an unsupported language, an oversized recording or a malformed WAV as a SpeechInputError so the loaded worker stays reusable.

orderModelSources: concurrent HEAD probes to every configured origin, the first 2xx wins and is returned first, all probes are joined and their bodies released, and a probe failure falls back to the configured order rather than failing.
Authenticated loopback HTTP server for the private worker: a timing-safe bearer-token compare, a POST /transcribe endpoint, a content-length bound, and 400 vs 500 separation for SpeechInputError.

The SenseVoiceWorker: a serial queue with maxPending, a bounded readiness frame read, a 32-byte random bearer token handed to the child via DSH_SPEECH_TOKEN, an idle timer that stops the worker, a step-keyed preparation state machine with progress throttling, and a dispose that aborts, joins the queue and terminates the worker.

Verified runtime assets: size+SHA-256 matching, download into a unique .part file that is hashed while streaming and then atomically renamed, partial-file cleanup on every failure path, and prepareRuntime's per-source fallback that stops on cancellation, storage failure or an unclassified error.

Child entry: parses argv[2] and the DSH_SPEECH_TOKEN, DELETES the token from its own environment, starts the loopback server, prints exactly one readiness line to stdout, and on a pre-readiness failure writes only the message to stderr and exits 1.

Vitest for classifyDownloadFailure: eleven nested error codes mapped to their reason, a TimeoutReason recognised as a timeout, a bare 'fetch failed' as network, an unknown code as unknown, and a cyclic cause chain terminating.

Vitest for createTranscriber with a mocked sherpa-onnx: language changes carried into the native config, VAD buffers copied for Electron, invalid language/format/oversize rejected, and the onset restoration applied to the first segment only and bounded by the padding window.

Vitest for prepareRuntime/inspectRuntime with a mocked asset lock: verified caches restored on every activation without a download, a missing or corrupted model/tokens/vad requiring preparation, platform-specific preparation, FP32 selection, cancellation, and source fallback on http/network/integrity but NOT on a local storage failure.

Opt-in real-inference e2e gated on DSH_SPEECH_E2E_ROOT/DSH_SPEECH_E2E_AUDIO env vars: prepares a real recognizer, transcribes cold then warm, asserts identical text, rejects an unsupported language, and asserts the worker was spawned only once.

Vitest for orderModelSources with controlled response barriers: first success wins, a faster HTTP error is ignored, configured order survives total failure, the probe deadline bounds without cancelling the download, and body cleanup is awaited.

Vitest for the private server: 401 on a missing or wrong token, 404 on an unknown path, 413 on an out-of-range content-length, a 200 transcript, and 400 vs 500 for a SpeechInputError versus a native failure.

Vitest for readReady and readTranscript: a fragmented readiness frame, malformed/oversized/invalid-port frames, exit-before-readiness, spawn failure, cancellation, a primitive abort reason, and marked input failures classified only on status 400/413.

Vitest for the bounded queue: a recording submitted during worker startup joins the queue, a third recording is refused with 'queue is full', and a waiting recording's cancellation stops it from ever reaching the worker.

Vitest for the plugin: lazy registration with no transcription until asked, the exact provider info and setup estimate, refusal of relative runtime/model/cache paths, and rejection of invalid download-source configuration.

Vitest for downloadAsset: verified files published and reused offline, altered downloads and HTTP failures leaving no partial file, credentials and query strings absent from the public message, the redirected source reported, and explicit cancellation distinguished from a preparation deadline.

Spawns the real worker entry with the tsx ESM hook and asserts six pre-readiness failure modes each exit 1 with an empty stdout, a newline-terminated stderr carrying only the message, and no stack trace.
One-line fixture that imports the shared worker.fixture.mjs so the source-launch test and the built-launch test use the same protocol peer.
Protocol fixture replacing the native recognizer: a real loopback HTTP server that honours the bearer token, appends each request's language to a file, and can hold, crash, or answer invalid-input.

The largest behavioural suite: worker warmth across recordings, manual download-source pinning, standby wake-up, queue bounds, disposal joining running and waiting requests, idle stop and reload, cancellation retention, recovery after a provider error or an unexpected worker exit, download-diagnostic publication and clearing, and the process-range reclamation after an unexpected idle exit.
